title: Harness of Minervini v2 ticker.cik response

examples: MINERVINI_SEC_USER_AGENT='Name email@example.com' scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline ticker cik AAPL

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

no_cache.description: Bypass both provider-cache reads and writes for this invocation.

limitations: SEC company_tickers.json is a mutable current snapshot. A symbol can be reassigned, so today's mapping is not evidence about who filed under it at a past session, and a historical --as-of is refused rather than answered from it.
Deciding that the identity held at the session being analysed stays the analyst's assertion, which is what ticker.fundamentals --cik records.
A symbol absent from the SEC list is unavailable rather than resolved; no name-similarity match is attempted.
Only filers appear here. A US-listed instrument with no SEC registrant -- and every non-filer -- has no CIK to return.
x-capability-contract.output: The current SEC company identity behind the symbol: its CIK and the registrant name filed under it.

status_meanings.ok: The symbol resolved to one SEC filing identity.
status_meanings.unavailable: The SEC list could not be read, does not carry this symbol, or was asked about a past session.

x-capability-contract.summary: Resolve a US-listed ticker to the SEC filing identity that ticker.fundamentals asks for by --cik.
